lenders.role: One of the nine lenders (Global Energy Monitor).

conditions: Financial close August 2010, first drawdown October 2010 (Global Energy Monitor). Thailand's EGAT agreed to buy 1,473 MW of about 1,800 MW for 25 years (Thailand Construction). A trade report on the financing says Thailand's state power utility EGAT "has agreed to purchase 1,473MW from the plant in accordance with the tariff MoU signed in May 2009" under a 25-year power purchase agreement, and that "About 100MW of power will be sold to Electricite du Laos for domestic consumption". The project cost "will be raised on a 75:25 debt to equity ratio", "The tenor of the loan is about 18 years", "The loan repayment starts one year from commencement of operations" and "The margins are on a step-up and step-down structure". The report says nothing about security, guarantees or conditions the nine Thai lenders set (Thailand Construction and Engineering News, 2010).
